# Records and export

`import metallurgypy.records`

Saving, reopening, verifying and exporting calculations.

## `Any`

```python
class Any(*args, **kwargs)
```

Special type indicating an unconstrained type.

- Any is assignable to every type.
- Any assumed to have all methods and attributes.
- All values are assignable to Any.

Note that all the above statements are true from the point of view of
static type checkers. At runtime, Any cannot be used with instance
checks.

## `Path`

```python
class Path(*args, **kwargs)
```

PurePath subclass that can make system calls.

Path represents a filesystem path but unlike PurePath, also offers
methods to do system calls on path objects. Depending on your system,
instantiating a Path will return either a PosixPath or a WindowsPath
object. You can also instantiate a PosixPath or WindowsPath directly,
but cannot instantiate a WindowsPath on a POSIX system or vice versa.

```python

```

Return the path as a URI.

### `Path.stat`

```python
stat(self, *, follow_symlinks=True)
```

Return the result of the stat() system call on this path, like
os.stat() does.

```python

```

Check if this path is a mount point


### `Path.rename`

```python
rename(self, target)
```

Rename this path to the target path.

The target path may be absolute or relative. Relative paths are
interpreted relative to the current working directory, *not* the
directory of the Path object.

Returns the new Path instance pointing to the target path.

### `Path.replace`

```python
replace(self, target)
```

Rename this path to the target path, overwriting if that path exists.

The target path may be absolute or relative. Relative paths are
interpreted relative to the current working directory, *not* the
directory of the Path object.

Returns the new Path instance pointing to the target path.

### `Path.symlink_to`

```python
symlink_to(self, target, target_is_directory=False)
```

Make this path a symlink pointing to the target path.
Note the order of arguments (link, target) is the reverse of os.symlink.

### `Path.hardlink_to`

```python
hardlink_to(self, target)
```

Make this path a hard link pointing to the same file as *target*.

Note the order of arguments (self, target) is the reverse of os.link's.

### `Path.expanduser`

## `Tolerances`

```python
class Tolerances(rel: float = 1e-09, abs: float = 1e-12) -> None
```

Relative and absolute tolerances for approximate comparisons.

The defaults are numerical choices, not physical constants. They sit far
above the rounding error accumulated by the handful of float64 operations
used in the current models (machine epsilon is about 2.2e-16) and far
below any realistic measurement precision. They are recorded in the
provenance of each result and can be overridden by the caller.

### `Tolerances.isclose`

```python
isclose(self, a: float, b: float) -> bool
```

True if ``a`` and ``b`` agree within the relative or absolute tolerance.

## `csv_safe`

```python
csv_safe(text: str) -> str
```

Neutralise spreadsheet formula injection in a *text* cell.

A cell that starts with ``= + - @`` (or a tab/CR) can be run as a formula when the CSV is
opened in a spreadsheet. Such text gets a leading apostrophe, unless it is just a number.
Never apply it to numeric cells.

## `dataclass`

```python
dataclass(cls=None, /, *, init=True, repr=True, eq=True, order=False, unsafe_hash=False, frozen=False, match_args=True, kw_only=False, slots=False, weakref_slot=False)
```

Add dunder methods based on the fields defined in the class.

Examines PEP 526 __annotations__ to determine fields.

If init is true, an __init__() method is added to the class. If repr
is true, a __repr__() method is added. If order is true, rich
comparison dunder methods are added. If unsafe_hash is true, a
__hash__() method is added. If frozen is true, fields may not be
assigned to after instance creation. If match_args is true, the
__match_args__ tuple is added. If kw_only is true, then by default
all fields are keyword-only. If slots is true, a new class with a
__slots__ attribute is returned.

## `save_record`

```python
save_record(path: str | os.PathLike[str], result: CalculationResult, *, name: str = '', notes: str = '', overwrite: bool = False, uncertainty: UncertainResult | None = None) -> Path
```

Save ``result`` with its inputs so it can be reopened and verified.

If ``uncertainty`` (from :func:`metallurgypy.precision.propagate_model`) is given,
the input uncertainties, correlations and propagated output uncertainties are stored too.

## `verify`

```python
verify(record: CalculationRecord, tolerances: Tolerances = Tolerances(rel=1e-09, abs=1e-12)) -> list[str]
```

Compare the stored outputs with a fresh calculation.

Returns a list of human-readable differences; an empty list means the saved
result is reproduced by the installed version of the model.
